visible_text.text:
THE MONTGOMERY ADVERTISER
Miss Capouya And Mr. Capouano Wed
Miss Selma Capouya became the bride of David Capouano at a fashionable ceremony which took place in the evening of June 8, at Temple Etz Ahayem. The ceremony was performed by Rabbi Eugene Blachschleger of Temple Beth-Or, and H. Ehrlich and Miss Martin Segall presented the nuptial music.
The ceremony took place under a canopy which had background of greenery. In the center were baskets filled with Ascension lilies and carnations. On either side were candelabra and white standard baskets filled with flowers. The front of the rostrum was outlined with baskets of flowers and ferns.
The bride wore an original Tafet model created of bridal satin cut on princess lines with long sleeves ending in points over the hands. The neckline was V-shape caught on either side with pearl clips. The bodice of the gown was fitted into a softly gathered girdle. The voluminous skirt extended into a lengthy train. The full length veil of illusion was attached to a coronet of pearls and net.
Miss Rita Capouya, sister of the bride, was maid of honor and Mrs. Morris Capouano, the groom's sister-in-law, was the matron of honor. Both wore gowns developed of silk marquisette over taffeta foundations in nile yellow with heart-shape necklines and long bishop sleeves. The bodice was form-fitting softly gathered in a wide girdle effect. The extremely full skirts were finished with deep peplums. They each wore matching hats adorned with flowers.
The bridesmaids included Misses Amelia Capilouto, of Atlanta, Fortune Capouya, Marie Capilouto, Regina Rousso of Atlanta, Clara Capouano, Pat Capouya. They wore similar gowns as the maid of honor in nile green.
Mr. Capouano chose his brother, Morris Capouano, as best man. Groomsmen were Isaac Hasson, Dr. Morris N. Capouya, Al Capouano, Albert Capouya, Morris Nelon and Joe Mussafer of Atlanta, Ga.
Mrs. Isaac Capouya, mother of the bride, wearing a blue lace gown, led the bridal procession, followed by the maid of honor and matron of honor.
The bride entered with her father, Isaac Capouya, and they were met at the altar by the bridegroom and the best man.
Immediately following the ceremony...
IS RECENT BRIDE: Mrs. David Capouano, before her marriage which took place June 8, at Temple Etz Ahayem, was Miss Selma Capouya, the wedding being an event of interest to the wide circle of the friends of the bride and groom.

CAPELOUTO Haïm, David Italien
Commerçant. Né à Rhodes le 25 mai 1905.
Il y est employé de bureau jusqu'au moment de son départ pour le Congo Belge. Arrivé à la Colonie par ses propres moyens, le 6 novembre 1926, il y est engagé pendant 5 mois par la firme « Franco », à Jadotville, puis il s'y installe commerçant à son compte. En juin 1932 il cesse son commerce et entre au service de la firme « Alzraki », à Jadotville, puis il passe à la maison « Amato Fres » où il reste jusqu'en juin 1938, ayant été détaché entretemps à Port Francqui et Kamina. Depuis 1938, il s'est installé commerçant à son compte à Mweka.
